intention: Every date and datetime the app creates resolves through one package, internal/clock, defaulting to America/Bogota, with a make tz-guard keeping it that way. Defaults only — the pgtype.Date UTC-midnight storage encoding and the per-user browser_tz cookie are untouched.
request:
Source ticket: MAG-20 — https://linear.app/magus-monitor/issue/MAG-20/datedate-time-time-zone
Project: architecture   Priority: Urgent

## Date/Date time Time Zone

* Analyze all date and date time created by the app (With golang code). The should be saved with Zone America/Bogota. Centralize a new logic that creates a date or date/time in that time zone.
* Update the CLAUDE/AGENTS instructtion or the best MD instructions per module to use that timezone convention. Find the best place that works for claude and opencode
* Find the best module to this kind of things that are cross-module. A new shared  util module sound like a good idea? I think it might work.. in the future we might have shared utilities for all modules

Acceptance Criteria

The app does not use UTC.

date and datetimes are centralized in one place and shared to all modules needed it

decisions.decision: Scope is defaults only: America/Bogota replaces every missing/fallback zone. The pgtype.Date UTC-midnight storage encoding and the per-user browser_tz cookie are both UNCHANGED. Zero migrations, zero backfill.
decisions.why: 'No UTC' means the default zone is never UTC, not that time.UTC vanishes. Rewriting the DATE encoding breaks the pgtype.Date contract and shifts day attribution; dropping the cookie undoes MAG-7.

decisions.decision: The package is internal/clock (stdlib time import only), not internal/util or an extension of internal/config.
decisions.why: One concern per package, named for it. ai/architecture.md:72 names the shared/common dump an anti-pattern. config is a cmd/-level concern; importing it from domain modules inverts the dependency direction.

decisions.decision: Full rule in ai/go-conventions.md next to the units rule; one-line non-negotiable in CLAUDE.md; NEW pointer to ai/go-conventions.md added to AGENTS.md for opencode.
decisions.why: go-conventions.md is in the base Doc-Pack, re-read by every worker and reviewer. AGENTS.md has no pointer to it today. Duplicating the rule drifts — CLAUDE.md is already 5 weeks newer than AGENTS.md.

decisions.decision: Sweep = 5 zone defaults + route ~8 raw time.Now() through clock.Now() + collapse the 4 duplicated UTC-midnight truncators into clock.CalendarDay. cmd/* is out of scope.
decisions.why: The 4 copy-pasted truncators are what AC#2 'centralized in one place' actually points at. Everything but the default change is behavior-preserving, so existing suites are the regression net. cmd/ is the composition root and loads the zone on purpose.

decisions.decision: Add make tz-guard (grep guard mirroring money-guard, // tz:allow: escape hatch) wired into make check, shipped in tier 7 LAST.
decisions.why: Wired in at tier 1 it fails on every unmigrated module; the alternatives are planting markers across all 5 modules (the one-big-change config.yaml forbids) or a red make check for six tiers.

decisions.decision: Unit tests: NEW coverage for internal/clock only. Tiers 2-6 add no new tests but MUST repair existing tests they break.
decisions.why: Narrows the owner's standing no-tests default by explicit choice. clock is pure, zero-dependency and depended on by all 5 other tiers; an off-by-one in CalendarDay shifts day attribution in telemetry, analytics and charging at once.

decisions.why: It spans 5 existing modules plus a new one. openspec/config.yaml's proposal rule forbids one big cross-module change and mandates a roadmap with one module-prefixed change per tier.
